explanation.headline: Ollama ships a fix for a model-import flaw that could write files outside its folder
explanation.whatHappened: Ollama, the tool that runs AI models on your own computer, published version 0.13.2. It fixes a security problem in how it imports model files, reported in a GitHub security advisory rated high severity.
explanation.previously: A specially crafted model file could make Ollama save data outside its own model folder when you imported it.
explanation.whatChanged: Ollama now checks every path inside an imported model and refuses anything that points outside the model folder.
explanation.whyItMatters: If you download models from places you do not fully trust, updating closes a way for a bad file to overwrite other files on your machine.
explanation.nextConfirmed: Version 0.13.2 is available now from the releases page.
explanation.nextSpeculative: Tools that bundle Ollama will likely pick up the fix in their next updates.

glossary.definition: A public notice describing a vulnerability, who is affected and how to fix it.
A trick where a file name like ../../ escapes the folder it should stay in.

explanation.analogy: It is like a mail room that used to accept any delivery address on a parcel and now only delivers inside the building.
explanation.intermediate: The import code joined archive entry names to the destination path without normalizing them. The patch resolves each path and rejects entries whose resolved location is outside the models directory.
explanation.technical: Fix in PR #9811 validates filepath.Rel(modelsDir, target) and rejects results beginning with "..". Affected: < 0.13.2. Advisory GHSA-7x2q-fixture, severity high.

explanation.headline: Vite 7.3 drops support for older Node.js versions and adds per-environment builds
explanation.whatHappened: Vite, a popular tool that bundles web apps, released version 7.3. The release notes mark a breaking change: it no longer runs on older Node.js versions.
explanation.previously: Projects could build with Vite on older Node.js releases that are near the end of their support.
explanation.whatChanged: Vite now requires a newer Node.js, and it adds an option to build different versions of an app for different environments.
explanation.whyItMatters: If your build machine runs an older Node.js, upgrading Vite will stop your builds until you update Node.js too.

glossary.definition: The program that runs JavaScript outside the browser, used by most web build tools.

explanation.intermediate: The engines field now excludes older Node.js lines. The new environment option lets one config produce separate client and server bundles.

explanation.headline: lnd merges a new way for node operators to set channel fees in bulk
explanation.whatHappened: The developers of lnd, a widely used Lightning Network node, merged a change that lets operators update fee settings for many payment channels at once.
explanation.previously: Operators had to update fees one channel at a time, and quick repeated updates could conflict.
explanation.whatChanged: A new command applies one fee policy to a group of channels and fixes the conflict between overlapping updates.
explanation.whyItMatters: Running a Lightning node gets less tedious. Note that this is merged code, not yet in a release you can install.
explanation.nextConfirmed: The change is merged into the main branch.
explanation.nextSpeculative: It would normally appear in the next lnd release.

glossary.definition: A system built on top of Bitcoin for fast, small payments.
Accepted into the main code, but not necessarily released to users.

explanation.analogy: Like changing the price on every shelf in a shop with one sign instead of relabelling each item.
explanation.intermediate: Adds a batch variant of the fee policy RPC and serializes policy updates per channel to avoid the race.
explanation.technical: PR #9502 introduces BatchUpdateChanPolicy and moves policy writes behind a per-channel mutex; fixes #9477.

explanation.headline: Claude Code patch release adds a timeout for slow hooks
explanation.whatHappened: Claude Code, a command-line coding assistant, published a small update that stops slow or stuck hooks from freezing a session.
explanation.previously: A hook that never finished could leave the tool waiting indefinitely.
explanation.whatChanged: Hooks now time out after a configurable limit, and the session continues with a warning.
explanation.whyItMatters: Teams that run checks through hooks get fewer stuck sessions.
